colleague (v1.76.0) is a Python headless coder-agent harness: one shared task runtime, many model backends behind it.
It turns backends (mock, vllm-openai, and out-of-tree plugins) into repo workers via a bounded tool loop, always returning the same typed TaskResult.

It turns backends (mock, vllm-openai, and out-of-tree plugins) into repo workers via a bounded tool loop, always returning the same typed TaskResult.
What it is for

Colleague solves the problem that AI coder backends are not interchangeable — a local vLLM model, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and a hosted assistant each bring their own SDK, controls, and output shape.
Colleague is the harness around the model: you point it at a repo task, pick a backend, and it runs the work through that backend's bounded tool-loop and hands back the same typed result every time.
Swap the backend and nothing else about your workflow changes.
It is explicitly **not** a chat assistant and **not** an IDE plugin — it is a headless task runtime meant to be scripted, gated, and audited.

Main parts and how they fit together
| Part | Where it lives | What it does |
| **Mind / backend** | `colleague/engines/` | The model/coder backend (mock, vllm-openai, or out-of-tree plugin) |

| **Adapter (Engine)** | `colleague/engine.py` | Abstract `Engine` with `work(task, config) -> TaskResult`; backends only supply how the model is called (a `complete` function) — they never re-implement the loop |

| **Task runtime / contract** | `colleague/contract.py` (+ `contract_records`, `contract_senses`, `contract_reports`, etc.) | Shared `Task` and `TaskResult` dataclasses with `to_dict`/`from_dict`; results round-trip through JSON unchanged |

| **Tool loop** | `colleague/loop.py` (+ 26 `loop_*` siblings) | Engine-agnostic bounded agentic loop; drives `complete` turns, executes tools via `ToolExecutor` against the repo, fires hooks at `task_start`/`pre_tool`/`post_tool`/`finish`, ends on `finish` or `max_steps` |
| **Plugins** | `colleague/registry.py` | Backends discovered via the `colleague.engines` entry-point group |
| **Run report** | `colleague/artifact.py` | JSON result artifact + step trace |
| **Telemetry** | `colleague/telemetry/` | Opt-in OpenTelemetry traces + metrics (lazy import, optional `[otel]` extra) |
| **Handoff** | `colleague/handoff.py` | Branch → commit → push → `gh pr create`, gated for offline/CI |
| **Doctor** | `colleague/oilcheck/` | Read-only configuration-readiness health check (`colleague doctor`) |
| **Approval gate** | `colleague/policy.py` | Operator-declared `.colleague/approvals.json` gating `run_command`, hooks, and command templates |
| **CLI** | `colleague/cli/__init__.py` | `main()` entry point, renders from an agentfront `App` |

**mock** — deterministic, networkless; the CI workhorse and reference against which a live backend's result shape is compared
**vllm-openai** — drives any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with tool calling; default model `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` ([pyproject.toml:115–117])

`colleague work "<goal>" --repo .` — run a task autonomously through a backend

`colleague doctor --probe` — check the install and ping the model endpoint
`colleague learn` / `colleague learn-from claude` — print a prompt teaching an agent to drive colleague / absorb another agent's skills

Install and run: `uv sync` then `uv run colleague ...`

Guard tests: `test_zero_deps.py` (no third-party runtime deps), `test_e2e_mock.py` (all-engines rule — mock and vllm-openai must produce identical result shape), `test_boundary.py` (subprocess/threading confined to sanctioned modules)

workledger-cli is an AgentCulture mesh-agent template: a dependency-free Python CLI whose only write verb appends one JSON entry at a time to an append-only JSONL ledger, so an agent can record its work, hand the ledger to subagents, and receive it back with their entries folded in — the whole tree of work and results stays traceable and checkable.
It is intentionally clonable: rename the package, edit `culture.yaml`, rewrite `CLAUDE.md`, and re-vendor only the skills you need.
Main parts and how they fit together:
Package `workledger/`: `__init__.py` exposes `__version__` (from importlib metadata); `__main__.py` is the `python -m workledger` entry that calls `workledger.cli:main`.

`workledger/cli/__init__.py`: builds the argparse parser, registers all verbs, pre-scans argv for `--json`, dispatches through `_dispatch`, and translates exceptions into structured `CliError` output — no tracebacks leak.
`workledger/cli/_errors.py`: `CliError` dataclass and the exit-code policy (0 success, 1 user error, 2 environment error, 3+ reserved).
`workledger/cli/_output.py`: strict split — results to stdout, errors/diagnostics to stderr; `--json` emits structured payloads on the same streams, never mixed.
`workledger/cli/_commands/`: one module per verb — `whoami`, `learn`, `explain`, `overview`, `doctor`, `append`, `list`, plus the `cli` noun group (`cli overview`) and the shared `_store.py`.
`workledger/cli/_commands/_store.py`: the core ledger store.

`append_entry()` stamps a uuid `id` and UTC `timestamp`, validates before any filesystem side effect, and appends exactly one line in append/O_CREAT mode — nothing rewrites, truncates, or deletes prior lines.
`iter_entries()` streams and validates every line (shape, timestamp format, unique ids), reporting corruption as exit 2 with a line number.
The ledger lives at `$WORKLEDGER_PATH`, defaulting to `.workledger/ledger.jsonl` under the git toplevel of the cwd (or the cwd itself outside a repo); `.workledger/` is git-ignored.
`workledger/explain/`: markdown catalog keyed by command-path tuples, backing `workledger-cli explain <path>`.

`culture.yaml` + `AGENTS.colleague.md`: mesh identity (suffix `workledger-cli`, backend `colleague`, pinned model); `doctor` verifies the prompt-file-present and backend-consistency invariants plus a skills-present check over the 18 vendored skills in `.claude/skills/` (cite-don't-import, sourced from guildmaster, devague, and colleague — see `docs/skill-sources.md`).

`tests/`: four modules — `test_ledger.py` (append/list, corruption, encoding, atomic short-write recovery, append-only guarantee), `test_cli.py` (version, help, unknown command, whoami/learn/explain), `test_cli_introspection.py` (overview/cli overview/doctor shapes), `test_sonar_pr_issues.py` (the SonarCloud PR-gating script).
Commands / entry points:
Console script `workledger-cli` → `workledger.cli:main` (`pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]`); also `python -m workledger`.
Every verb supports `--json`.

Verbs: `whoami` (identity from culture.yaml), `learn` (self-teaching prompt), `explain <path>` (markdown docs), `overview` (agent snapshot), `doctor` (identity invariants), `append <json>`/`--stdin` (only write; required `agent`/`action`/`summary`, optional `refs`/`data`; `id`/`timestamp` generated, unknown or generated fields rejected), `list` (`--agent`, `--action`, `--since`, `--limit`), `cli overview` (CLI surface).
Build and test:
Built with hatchling, `requires-python >=3.12`, `dependencies = []` (runtime is self-contained; `teken>=0.8` is dev-only).
Dev group: pytest, pytest-xdist, pytest-cov, bandit, flake8, isort, black, teken.

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`): `uv run pytest -n auto --cov=workledger ...`, SonarCloud scan (when `SONAR_TOKEN` is set), black/isort/flake8/bandit/markdownlint, the `teken cli doctor . --strict` agent-first rubric gate, and a version-bump check on PRs.
`.github/workflows/publish.yml`: TestPyPI on PRs, PyPI on push to main, both via Trusted Publishing; quality gate `sonar.qualitygate.wait=true`.
Coverage floor 60% (`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 60`).

It is not a chat assistant or IDE plugin; you point it at a repo task, pick a backend, and it runs the work through that backend's bounded tool loop and hands back the same typed result every time.
What it is for

Reproducible, auditable, backend-agnostic AI coding tasks: every run writes a JSON result artifact (`.colleague/<task-id>.json`) with a full step trace, always-on work stats, and opt-in OpenTelemetry telemetry.
It includes operator controls — command templates, lifecycle hooks, an approval gate, git/PR handoff, and a read-only `doctor` health check.
Main parts and how they fit together

**Task contract** (`colleague/contract.py`): plain dataclasses `Task` and `TaskResult` with `to_dict`/`from_dict`, so every engine consumes a `Task` and produces a `TaskResult` of the *same shape* regardless of which model ran underneath.
The artifact is just `TaskResult.to_dict()` serialized.
**Engine protocol** (`colleague/engine.py`): `Engine` ABC with `work(task, config) -> TaskResult`.
Backends are adapters — they know how to invoke and control one model but speak the shared contract on both ends.
They do **not** re-implement the loop; they supply a `complete` callable and delegate to `colleague.loop.run`.

**Bounded tool loop** (`colleague/loop.py` + `colleague/loop_*.py` lanes): engine-agnostic loop driven by a `complete` callable, ending on `finish`, an empty tool-call turn, or the `max_steps` budget.
It fires hooks at `task_start`/`pre_tool`/`post_tool`/`finish`; only `pre_tool` is control-bearing (allow/deny/rewrite).
**Two backends** registered under the `colleague.engines` entry-point group (an out-of-tree plugin uses the same mechanism):
`mock` (`colleague/engines/mock.py`): deterministic, networkless, writes a `colleague-mock.md` marker then finishes; the CI workhorse and contract reference.

`vllm-openai` (`colleague/engines/vllm_openai.py`): drives any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint via stdlib `urllib` (no vendor SDK); default model `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`; retargeting a server is a config change, not a code change.
**CLI** (`colleague/cli/`): `colleague.cli:main` (also `clg`; `python -m colleague` via `colleague/__main__.py`).

A single `work` call exercises most of the runtime in this order [w11]:
**Backend/plugin resolution** — `--engine <name>` resolves to an adapter via the `colleague.engines` entry-point group (`colleague/registry.py`).

Every engine consumes a `Task` and produces a `TaskResult` of identical shape.

**Engine adapter** — `colleague/engine.py` defines `Engine.work(task, config) -> TaskResult`; an engine only supplies *how the model is called* (a `complete` function) and delegates to `colleague.loop.run`.
**Tool loop** — `colleague/loop.py` (the entry point) plus 26 `loop_*` siblings runs the bounded agentic turn loop over repo-confined tools in `colleague/tools.py` + `tool_schemas`.

**Tool set** — ten tools exposed as OpenAI function schemas: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `list_dir`, `run_command`, `culture`, `devague`, `subagent`, `subagents`, `finish` (`edit_file` is a partial-edit primitive; `run_command` runs with `cwd` pinned to the root).

Every engine inherits these for free via the loop (the "all-engines rule").

**Layered per-model config** — `colleague/layers.py` composes AGENTS + skills into a model-specific system prompt on `Engine.system_prompt()`; a per-model hooks overlay (`.colleague/<model>/hooks.json`) layers ahead of base hooks.

**Write isolation** — `colleague/worktrees.py`: each `work`/`drive` runs in a throwaway worktree at HEAD; the operator's tree is never touched.

It serves the operator headless (`associate run`) or as the mesh resident (`culture start associate`), and mesh peers such as colleague hand it work over IRC [w5].
**Main parts and how they fit together.** The Python package `associate/` (no third-party dependencies at base; `server` and `mcp` extras are optional) [w6]:

`cli/` — unified entry point `associate.cli:main`, also `python -m associate`; commands: `whoami`, `learn`, `explain <path>`, `overview`, `doctor`, `cli overview`, `run [prompt]`, `bench`, `runs start|show|list`, `serve`, `tokens issue|list|revoke`, `mcp` [w4][w5][w10].
Every command takes `--json`; results to stdout, errors/diagnostics to stderr; exit codes 0/1/2/3+ [w5].

Colleague (v1.76.0, Apache-2.0, Python ≥3.12) is a headless, swappable coder-agent harness: one shared task runtime that turns different model backends into repo workers ("one runtime, many minds").
It is explicitly not a chat assistant or IDE plugin.

A caller runs `colleague work "<goal>" --repo <path>` against a chosen backend; the backend executes a bounded agentic tool-loop in the target repo and returns a uniform typed TaskResult, and the run is handed off as a branch/commit/PR with a JSON result artifact.
Main parts and fit: (1) Backend/mind — a model (vLLM, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
(2) Adapter — colleague/engine.py's Engine ABC, work(task, config) -> TaskResult; adapters delegate the loop to colleague/loop.py and only supply how the model is called (a complete callable).

(3) Two bundled backends registered under the colleague.engines entry-point group: mock (deterministic, networkless, CI workhorse) and vllm-openai (OpenAI /v1/chat/completions over stdlib urllib); out-of-tree plugins use the same entry-point mechanism, discovered by colleague/registry.py (the all-engines rule: contract behavior binds every backend identically).
(4) Task runtime/contract — colleague/contract.py plus split siblings (contract_records, contract_senses, etc.) defining Task and TaskResult with to_dict/from_dict so results round-trip through JSON.

(5) Bounded tool-loop — colleague/loop.py (split into ~26 loop_* siblings under a 1000-line ceiling, loop.py stays the entry point) over repo-confined tools in colleague/tools.py (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, grep_search, glob, run_command, culture, finish); guaranteed termination via finish / empty-tool-call turn / max_steps (default 25).
(6) Run report — colleague/artifact.py writes .colleague/<task-id>.json with the step trace and always-on WorkStats.

(7) Extensibility owned by the loop/runtime, not backends: lifecycle hooks (.colleague/hooks.json), command templates (.colleague/commands/*.md), interactive palette (colleague session), layered per-model AGENTS/skills config, approval gate (colleague/policy.py via .colleague/approvals.json), telemetry (opt-in OpenTelemetry, colleague/telemetry/), git/PR handoff (colleague/handoff.py: branch→commit→push→gh pr create, gated so --no-pr/no remote stays local), doctor (colleague/oilcheck/, colleague doctor), and write isolation (throwaway worktrees).

coherence-cli — repository explanation
What it is for
**coherence-cli** (v0.6.1, Apache-2.0) is an **agent-first CLI** for measuring and maintaining coherence in agentic systems.

It turns context, claims, meaning, provenance, and behavioral traces into inspectable, reproducible signals so an agent (or a mesh consumer such as colleague, steward, eidetic, or taskmaster) can decide whether to trust an artifact, refresh it, repair it, route it, or remember it — instead of treating a lone number as ground truth.

Every measurement is **honest about what it could and could not verify**: rule-based diagnostics run offline (no model, no network, no `datetime.now()` — age is computed against a supplied reference date), and absence of evidence lowers confidence rather than inflating a score.
Each score is declared **model-relative and anchor-defined** (relative to the embedding model, endpoint, and anchor set that produced it), never model-independent.

It is part of the **AgentCulture mesh**: `culture.yaml` declares `suffix: coherence-cli` / `backend: claude`, with a matching `CLAUDE.md` prompt file, and 11 vendored guildmaster skills under `.claude/skills/`.
The five coherence domains
Each domain lives in its own package under `coherence/`:
| Domain | Question it answers | What it ships |

| **quality** | Can this context/claim be trusted right now, without a model call? | Offline rule-based freshness/provenance/fidelity heuristics, each in `[0,1]` with confidence and can't-verify diagnostics (`source_liveness_unverified`, `publication_date_unverified`, `no_dateable_statements`, …). |

| **meaning** | What semantic structure does this artifact carry? | The **Meaning Gradient**: anchor-axis projection over sentence embeddings → `meaning_score` + five subdimensions (consequence, agency, causality, affordance, future_constraint), plus rule-based offline diagnostics (`missing_consequence`, `missing_owner`, `missing_next_action`). Needs an embedding endpoint (`COHERENCE_EMBED_URL` / `COHERENCE_EMBED_MODEL`); unreachable → exit 2 with a hint, diagnostics still run. |

| **signal** | How do measurements behave over time? | Source-agnostic series analysis: `trend` (f′/f″, monotonicity, volatility), `pattern` (six motifs), `resonance` (signed Pearson per field pair — positive = resonance, negative = interference, one code path), `forecast` (labeled naive extrapolation), `collect` (build a series from any domain's score JSONs). Mixed-frame guard warns when comparing points measured under different frames. |

| **investiture** | Did this artifact's meaning become a durable causal imprint? | Estimated micro-investiture (`investiture_score = meaning_density × agency_coupling × future_constraint × affordance`) via `coherence.meaning` (no duplicate embed path). Always `mode: "estimated"`; persistence/integration/behavioral-effect explicitly `None` with a `missing_behavioral_outcome` diagnostic. |

| **frames** | From which coordinate frame was this measurement taken? | `frames inspect <measurement.json>` (frame completeness: complete/partial/absent) and `frames diff <a> <b>` (gauge-comparability, differing fields named). Every embedding-derived score carries a `frame` block (model, endpoint, anchor set, axes, projection method). |

Plus an **assess** multi-domain verb (`coherence assess <file>`) that runs quality (always), meaning (if the embed endpoint is up), and investiture (if meaning ran), returning one report that honestly names which domains were available/unavailable — partial availability is a normal success, not an error.
How the parts fit together
**`coherence/schema.py`** — the shared measurement envelope.

Every new-domain noun emits exactly five top-level keys: `domain`, `score_type`, `scores` (open name→number map), `frame` (dict / `None` / null-frame dict, key always present), `diagnostics` (`[{code, message}]`).
Validation is strict (machine-readable `EnvelopeError` codes).
**Two-speed adoption rule**: new nouns (`quality`, `signal`, `investiture`, `assess`) emit the full envelope from day one.

Existing `meaning` verbs keep their pinned v0.5.0 top-level shape (`meaning_score`, `subdimensions`, `diagnostics`) and gain only additive `domain`/`score_type`/`frame` keys — never reshaped implicitly.

**`coherence/cli/__init__.py`** — unified CLI entry point (`main()`), argparse with a structured error parser, dispatch that catches `CliError` and unknown exceptions, exit codes 0/1/2, stdout/stderr split via `coherence/cli/_output.py`.

**`coherence/cli/_commands/`** — one `register(sub)` module per noun/verb: `whoami`, `learn`, `explain`, `overview`, `doctor`, `cli`, `meaning` (score/compare/trend), `quality` (score/compare, optional `--reference-date`), `signal` (collect/trend/pattern/resonance/forecast), `investiture` (score/compare), `frames` (inspect/diff), `assess`.

**`coherence/assess.py`** — the multi-domain engine behind `assess`; threads an injectable `embed_fn` (defaults to the real HTTP `embed_texts`) through meaning and investiture, never calls `datetime.now()`, and never raises for domain unavailability.
**`coherence/meaning/embed.py`** — env-configured client for an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint; the lobes gateway serves an `embedder` role discoverable via `GET /capabilities`.
**`scripts/refresh_meaning_vectors.py`** — refreshes recorded embedding-vector fixtures so CI runs with zero network access.

**`docs/`** — `domains.md`, `envelope.md`, `signal-series.md`, `meaning-gradient-live-tests.md`, `skill-sources.md`, plus `specs/` and `plans/` (the converged devague specs and build plans behind the 0.6.0 restructure).
**`.eidetic/memory`** — in-repo, public eidetic memory shared with mesh peers.
Commands / entry points
**Console script**: `coherence` → `coherence.cli:main` (declared in `pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]`).
**Module entry**: `python -m coherence` → `coherence/__main__.py`.
**Global verbs**: `whoami`, `learn`, `explain <path>`, `overview`, `doctor`, `cli overview`.

**Domain verbs**: `meaning {score,compare,trend}`, `quality {score,compare [--reference-date]}`, `signal {collect,trend,pattern,resonance,forecast}`, `investiture {score,compare}`, `frames {inspect,diff}`, `assess <file>`.
Every verb supports `--json`; results to stdout, errors/diagnostics to stderr, never mixed.
**Exit codes**: `0` success, `1` user-input error, `2` environment error, `3+` reserved.
Failures raise `CliError` with a structured `{code, message, remediation}` shape; no Python traceback leaks to stderr.

**Build**: `pyproject.toml` uses **hatchling**, packages `["coherence"]`, Python `>=3.12`.
**Runtime deps**: `numpy>=1.26`, `httpx>=0.27`.
**Dev deps**: `pytest`, `pytest-xdist`, `pytest-cov`, `bandit`, `flake8`, `isort`, `black`, `teken`.
**Dev setup**: `uv sync`.
**Tests**: `uv run pytest -n auto` (CI adds `--cov=coherence`).
665 tests, **all offline in CI** (recorded fixtures, no network).
**Lint (CI `lint` job)**: `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, `flake8`, `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r coherence`, `markdownlint-cli2`, and the agent-first rubric gate `teken cli doctor . --strict`.
**Version policy** (CI `version-check` job on PRs): every PR must bump `pyproject.toml` version, else it fails.
**CI** (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`): runs on push/PR to `main` via `ubuntu-latest`, Python 3.12 via `astral-sh/setup-uv`, with optional SonarCloud quality gate when `SONAR_TOKEN` is set.
**Publish** (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`): `uv build` + `uv publish` with **PyPI Trusted Publishing**; TestPyPI on PRs (from the same repo), real PyPI on push to `main`.

culture-rules — repository explanation
What it is for
`culture-rules` (version 0.47.0) is the **rules engine for the AgentCulture mesh**: rules → conditions → workflows → actions, carried out by actors (agents, humans, code, services, robots).

It is a Python library, `culture_rules`, with a CLI, an HTTP API, an MCP server, an engine node, and a graph-first React Flow visual editor with four tabs: Workflows | Actors | Variables | Statistics.[w4]
It serves two readers in one system:
**The operator**, composing and supervising automation across the hosts spark, thor and spark2 from a browser at rules.culture.dev.
**Mesh agents**, driving the same rules, workflows and actors through the `culture-rules` CLI and MCP server.

Its purpose: one graphical, agent-operable place to decide when work happens, how it flows across machines and who does it, that keeps working when one machine falters — so automation is not per-host glue only its author understands.[w4] The mesh resident (declared in `culture.yaml`) is the `claude` backend for the `culture-rules` agent.[w16]
Main parts and how they fit together
**`culture_rules/` library (dependency-free core)** — standard-library only; the CLI, API, MCP server and node are thin layers over it.[w4][w7]
`model/` — the data model: rules, triggers, conditions, workflows, steps, actions, variables, actors, machines, placement, refs, validation and serialization.

`engine/` — the run executor: every run is one persisted state-machine document in the store; each tick re-reads the document, applies exactly one transition and writes it back with compare-and-set on `rev`, keeping no run state in memory.[w11]

This is the **culture** repo (CULTURE.DEV, v14.18.0): the integrated workspace and canonical CLI for a professional mesh of collaborating AI agents, built on the AgentIRC IRC-native runtime.

It ships one Python distribution (build backend hatchling, requires Python ≥3.12, managed with uv) containing two packages: a thin `culture` front-door and the in-tree `culture_core` engine (merged back in the 14.0.0 release, issue #462).
Both `culture` and `culture-core` console scripts entry-point to `culture_core.cli:main`, and `python -m culture` works too.
Main parts

**`culture/`** — only `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`; the `__init__` installs a meta-path finder that aliases every `culture.<x>` import to the identical `culture_core.<x>` module object (module identity), so `culture.x is culture_core.x`.

**`culture_core/`** — the engine: `agentirc` (thin re-export shim over the external `agentirc-cli` dependency, which is the actual IRCd), per-backend agent clients under `clients/` (claude, codex, colleague, copilot, acp, plus shared), `protocol` (IRC command/message/reply extensions over RFC 2812), `bots` (bot manager, system bots incl. welcome bot), `cli` (all command groups), `telemetry`, `doctor`, `overview`, `sandbox`, `skills` (vendored `communicate` and `culture`), `persistence`, `config`, etc.
**`protocol/`** at repo root, **`plugins/`** (claude-code, codex), **`tests/`** (134 test files), **`docs/`**, and a root `culture.yaml` agent identity config.
Commands / entry points

The CLI (`culture_core.cli.main`) offers noun-based groups — `agents`, `server`, `mesh`, `channel`, `bot`, `skills`, `devex`, `afi`, `secret`, `console`, `introspect`, `doctor`, `residents`, `sandbox` — plus universal verbs `explain`/`overview`/`learn`.

`culture server start` embeds the agentirc IRCd in-process and installs culture's system-bot bridge; verbs like `restart`, `link`, `logs`, `version`, `serve` fall through verbatim to `agentirc.cli.dispatch`.
Agent harnesses (claude/codex/colleague/copilot/acp) live in the sibling `cultureagent` package.
